title: The Lighter Brief
overview: It's a soggy Thanksgiving Eve around Charlotte, with rain and wind sticking around into Thursday morning before sunshine returns for Black Friday. Elsewhere, Cardi B gave a heartfelt award speech, Popcaan's first US shows drew a staggering ticket queue, and a medieval sculpture stolen in 1979 is finally heading home. There's also a Caribbean dry-season outlook, a political row in Jamaica, and a couple of interesting research findings.

stories.headline: Rainy, windy start to Thanksgiving in Charlotte, then sunshine
stories.summary: A strong storm system moving up the East Coast is bringing heavy rain and gusty winds to the Charlotte area through Thanksgiving morning. Showers should linger early Thursday, then gradually clear in the afternoon. Friday and the weekend look mostly dry and sunny.
key_facts: Overnight wind gusts of 40 to 50 mph are possible
Thanksgiving afternoon highs are expected in the 50s
Friday looks mostly sunny and breezy, with highs in the lower 50s
Sunday could reach the lower 60s, with a stray shower possible
stories.why: If you're on the road Wednesday night or Thursday morning, plan for wet roads and slower driving. The good news is the holiday afternoon and weekend clear up nicely.

stories.headline: Overturned truck narrows Monroe Expressway westbound
stories.summary: A tractor-trailer went through a guardrail and was left hanging over a bridge on the westbound Monroe Expressway near Rocky River Road in Unionville on Wednesday morning. At first, all westbound lanes were closed. Traffic was cut to one lane around noon while crews worked to lift the truck.
key_facts: The crash happened around 11:20 a.m. on Wednesday, Nov. 25
It was near Exit 260 on westbound US 74 in Union County
NCDOT urged drivers to avoid the area
disputed: The cause of the crash, whether anyone was hurt, and how long the lanes will stay closed were not yet known
stories.why: If you're heading west through Union County for the holiday, an alternate route could save you some time.

stories.headline: Charlotte airport travelers report mostly smooth Thanksgiving trips
stories.summary: Thanksgiving Eve was busy at Charlotte Douglas, but travelers said things were going relatively smoothly. Some arrived two to three hours early to stay ahead of the wind and rain. Others said they were keeping a Plan B in mind after an FAA ground stop a few weeks ago.
key_facts: Nearly 2 million passengers are expected through Charlotte Douglas over the holiday travel period
One traveler said the airport felt less busy than in previous years
Officials advise arriving early and checking with your airline for delays
stories.why: So far, holiday travel through Charlotte is going better than many people feared.

stories.headline: Cardi B's 'go get it' speech, plus a shout-out to Summer Walker
stories.summary: Cardi B received the first-ever Global Woman of the Year award at the Billboard Canada Women in Music Awards in Toronto. In her speech, she encouraged women to chase their goals and to appreciate who they already are. She also warmly thanked Summer Walker, who won the Global Visionary Award that night, for supporting her 'publicly and privately.'
key_facts: The ceremony was held Tuesday, Nov. 24, at Rebel in Toronto
Cardi listed her year: a new album, a fourth child, a sold-out arena tour, and a hair care business, Grow Good
She received surprise video messages from Missy Elliott, Lizzo, and Charlamagne tha God
disputed: Everything here is confirmed. These are on-stage remarks reported by multiple outlets.
stories.why: It's a nice moment of artists publicly lifting each other up.

stories.headline: Jamaica's opposition renews call for disaster agency chief to resign
stories.summary: Jamaica's opposition People's National Party held a protest in Kingston calling for ODPEM Director General Commander Alvin Gayle to step down. The protest followed an Auditor-General's report on how Hurricane Melissa relief donations were managed. Opposition spokesperson Damion Crawford said both Gayle and the government should be held accountable.
key_facts: The audit says a significant number of container houses can't be accounted for
It also found donated funds were used for purposes other than intended, and some stored food spoiled past its best-before date
The protest took place Wednesday in Cross Roads, Kingston
disputed: The resignation call comes from the opposition. The article does not include a response from Gayle or the government.
stories.why: The dispute is about whether hurricane aid reached the people it was meant for, which matters to many Jamaicans.

stories.headline: Caribbean told to prepare for a drier, hotter dry season
stories.summary: A climatologist at the Caribbean Institute for Meteorology and Hydrology says a strong El Niño is likely to bring drier conditions, more heat, and warmer seas during the 2026/2027 dry season. The eastern and southern Caribbean are seen as most vulnerable. He noted that rain will be less frequent but could still come in intense bursts, so people should keep following their local weather services.
key_facts: The warning came from Dr Cédric J Van Meerbeeck of the Barbados-based CIMH
El Niño means unusually warm ocean temperatures in the equatorial Pacific
Record or near-record warmth often follows in the year after an El Niño begins
stories.why: An early heads-up gives governments and households time to plan for water use and heat.

stories.headline: Gastonia warming center set to open on cold nights from Dec. 7
stories.summary: The City of Gastonia, Gaston County, and City Church are opening a warming center for people experiencing homelessness this winter. It will open on nights when the forecast is 32 degrees or colder. Some residents had worried it wouldn't be ready before the first freeze, but it has now cleared the required regulations.
key_facts: The location is City Church's Unity Campus, 482 N. Myrtle School Road
Hours are 8 p.m. to 7 a.m., with on-site security, from Dec. 7 through March 31
Officials will decide 48 hours ahead whether to open, based on National Weather Service forecasts
stories.why: Neighbors teaming up so everyone has a warm place to sleep on freezing nights is a lovely bit of community.

stories.headline: Popcaan's first US concerts spark a 350,000-fan ticket queue
stories.summary: After nearly 20 years without a US visa, dancehall star Popcaan will finally perform in the United States, at Brooklyn's Barclays Center. The Dec. 27 show sold out within an hour, so promoters added a second night. The online queue for that show passed 350,000 people.
key_facts: Shows are on Dec. 27 and 28 at Barclays Center
The arena holds about 19,000 for concerts
Popcaan has collaborated with Drake, Jamie xx, and Gorillaz
stories.why: It's a long-awaited moment for Popcaan and his fans, and a big one for dancehall.
